items.reader: The document doesn't recommend shipping. It escalates. The Test arm (new ranker plus `snippet_length` changed from 160 to 220) raised Successful Search Rate by +0.81% relative, and all four guardrails pass. But the snippet change was not pre-registered and has no audit record, so the lift can't be attributed to the ranker. Don't claim the ranker works yet. First decide whether the bundle (ranker plus 220-character snippets) is the intended launch. If it is, the evidence supports shipping it. If not, re-run with `snippet_length` held at 160 in both arms. Also settle whether the 0.005 bar is relative or absolute. Successful Search Rate relative lift of +0.81% (0.4120 → 0.4153, 95% CI +0.41% to +1.21%). The unit is relative percent change in the rate. The point estimate clears a relative 0.5% bar, but the CI's lower bound (+0.41%) does not. The document doesn't mention this. The confound. A second change shipped in the same arm, with no record of who made it or why, so the primary result can't isolate the ranker. Secondary metrics (CTR, Long Click Rate, Clicks per User) are flat and don't corroborate the lift. Segment p<0.05 results are unplanned cuts without multiplicity correction. Desktop success is negative (-0.66%, p=0.11).
